title: Futureproof Model Compatibility Index and Entitlements Playbook
creator: Ethan Li
description:
Context: As Redwood expands enterprise sales for Dedicated and Private, procurement decisions increasingly hinge on two orthogonal signals: technical compatibility (quantization, kernel availability, latency on target hardware, toolchain maturity) and commercial entitlements (licensing, redistributability, region restrictions). This ticket creates a repeatable, data-driven "Model Compatibility Index (MCI)" and an Entitlements Checklist that together produce a single procurement-ready score and a short checklist for Sales/Legal/Infra.

Scope: 1) Define MCI inputs and scoring rules (performance, quantization support, verifier status, memory footprint, KV-cache friendliness, fallback variant availability). 2) Define entitlements checklist (redistribution rights, on-prem allowance, export controls, SSO/KMS compatibility). 3) Implement a lightweight scoring spreadsheet + Confluence playbook and a JSON schema for downstream automation (score + flags). 4) Run a pilot to score the top 12 models currently in our catalog and surface results to Sales and Capacity Planning.

Deliverables: - Confluence Playbook: scoring rubric, checklist, fallbacks for high-risk items - CSV/Sheet with per-model scores and normalized category breakdowns - One-pager for Sales: how to interpret scores when negotiating Dedicated/Private contracts - API proto-spec (JSON schema) for Engineering to pull scores into provisioning flows - Pilot review meeting notes and recommended next steps
acceptance_criteria: MCI rubric documented in Confluence with example calculations for 3 models
Entitlements checklist validated with Legal on two representative contract clauses
Pilot spreadsheet populated for 12 models with at least one high/medium/low bucket identified
JSON schema published in repo and agreed by ENG owners for downstream automation
Sales one-pager reviewed and accepted by the Sales lead (email confirmation or Confluence sign-off)
decisions: MCI will use a weighted sum with default weights: performance 30%, memory/footprint 20%, kernel maturity 20%, quant-fallback 15%, community signals 15% (weights adjustable via a settings table in the playbook)
Entitlements checklist will be binary flags (allowed/conditional/forbidden) with an explanatory note; conditional flags require Legal review
Pilot scoring will be run offline in a shared spreadsheet; Engineering will be asked to convert the final rubric to a JSON schema for automation
Score thresholds: 75+ => Ready for Dedicated sales; 50-74 => Private subject to Legal and infra checks; <50 => Requires remediation or alternative model selection
